Frere Hospital handover

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Delivery

Show:

Summary:
In September the "Making a Differennce" campaign will hand over a paediatric ward and operating facility at Frere Hospital in the Eastern Cape. Thought to be the first operating theatre in the Eastern Cape that will be used to bring life saving surgery to children.

Viewing Notes:
13/11/2014 04:50:52 PM – GM, Karolina, WG, AC
Carol: viewing Frere

Need to see your promos please before you finalise – at least email the script to Amalia and Wynand. Prefer to see them properly when we view again.
No empathy for the case studies – too abrupt
None of the previous campaign material
The minister of health is still the current minister – and take him out
And take out all other campaign montages with other hand overs we have done – you show things not linked to East London
You don’t show us any before shots of the theatres – the old fashioned theatres.
You show a shot from a messy room down a passage and its unrelated
When you show Bongani with his first link in the theatre we are not seeing the theatre – we see recovery rooms and other things
There are two theatres and they are visually distinctly different
You are focussing too much on the irrelevant rooms and not enough on the theatres and the technology in them which is remarkable.
FOCUS: going from what was there and what was given but the technology is on an entirely different level in each room and we have detailed explanation of the equipment in each room. You need to take sound ups of all the bits of technology.
Include the fact that there wer 47 or 50 donors in total in voice.
You said the MEC handed over the theatre and she didn’t it was handed over to her by us.
Show more of the plaques of the other sponsors who are not interviewed as we need to show more of them.
There is a bit of a disconnect between the burns and hernia patient – explain how they are linked through the facility being able to accommodate both.
Include Bongani’s interviews with people like the archetects to explain the state of the art modern facility.
Make Chirnis’ title professor and intro him as such.

Coltman still spelt wrong
Funded by CB Tust. Rather say created by the CB Making a difference Trust
Braam van der Hoven not Hover

Leave all logos out

Use same word consistently: stick to making a Difference Trust rather than campaign.
Admission and recover ward. Rather call it area. Other rooms are UTILITY ROOMS

Press Release:


Top Tech for Frere
East London’s Frere Hospital serves some of the country’s most desperate communities. When Carte Blanche visited the hospital in 2011, children were being operated on in under-resourced adult theatres while an abandoned operating theatre suite was being used as a storage facility. Funded by the Carte Blanche Making a Difference Campaign, the hospital now boasts two new state of the art dedicated paediatric operating theatres complete with Recovery and Nurses stations, management offices, sterilisation rooms and more.


Script:


Frere Handover Script

Making a Difference TRUST ( Not campaign – check in case I missed one)

V/O
This is Akhuna Ndahala and her 3 year old daughter Yolanda, who live on the outskirts of East London.

Akuna
Our shack burnt down from 10 – 11 oclock.

V/O
Her daughter suffered severe 3rd degree burns. She has been in hospital for the past 3 weeks and she is scheduled to have skin grafts in theatre today.

Up Sound Dr Chitnis

“These are the 6 cases which have been booked…”

“This is a baby who has hot water burns and who had a skin graft.”


V/O
These are the new state of the art paediatric operating theatres at Frere Hospital in East London that were created by Carte Blanche’s Making a Difference Trust. The campaign raised 14 million rand to bring hope and better medical care to children like Yvonne.

V/O
It was a very different picture when Carte Blanche featured Frere Hospital three years ago, in a story which high lighted the general decline of the hospital. This discarded ward housed a fully functional operating theatre, but due to lack of resources it had become neglected and fell into disuse.

Dr Siva Pillay Superintendent-General of Health in the province at the time showed us around.

Dr Siva Pillay (Superintendent General: Eastern Cape Health Department): ‘There’s no money, no surgeons and it was just closed down.’

Derek Watts (Carte Blanche presenter): ‘This is the state it’s gotten to?’

Dr Pillay: ‘It got to this stage. Now it’s used by electrical people as a storeroom.’

Dr Pillay: ‘When I came in it was a bankrupt department, riddled with corruption and with a lot of ineffective managers and a totally demoralised workforce.’

V/O
And with a situation like that the needs of the patients were compromised.
When Carte Blanche through the Making a Difference Trust approached the department to help upgrade their facilities, they were turned down.


V/O
Under Dr Pillay’s tenur however things changed. Carte Blanche Executive Producer George Mazarakis and the patron of the Making A Difference Trust, Karolina Andropoulus, met with the hospital in East London to discuss their needs. Nestle generously donated R 1.5 million to kick-start the refurbishment of the paediatric theatres.

Link
“When Carte Blanche visited Frere Hospital in 2011 this was a discarded theatre, it was being used as a store room but has not been used as a fully functioning operating theatre since the 1950’s looking at it now that’s quite extra ordinary.”


V/O
Dr Itayi Simango is the surgeon on duty today, his first operation of the day was a hernia repair on a 6 month old child.

“Everything went reasonably well and he is being recovered by the aneathetists as you can see.”

Up sound “Good boy”

“I am so grateful for what they have done, because the children have been suffering.”

Voice ( revoice link)

Thanks to the Making A Difference Trust this is the first dedicated paediatric operating theatre in the Eastern Cape, previously children’s operations were performed in the adult theatres in the Province.
But….( See if this works)


Link
Now they will be able to get timeous assistance in these state of the art facilities.

V/O
Dr Rolene Wagner is the CEO at Frere.

Dr Wagner
“At the moment the waiting list is five months for the child to be operated on. So by having two dedicated theatres we can now increase the operating time and start working down the waiting list. So it’s going to make a huge difference it can potentially save lives but it can also improve quality of life of that child because you are intervening sooner rather than later.”


V/O
It ‘s just before 2 o’clock and the Yolanda is waiting to go into the theatre.


Akhuna

“I am very happy because my child will be operated today and life will be better for her.”

V/O
Yolanda has an excellent chance for a good recovery with a dedicated medical team and these first world facilities.

Dr Simango

“We will be harvesting skin from her thighs and covering the burnt areas and both the donor area and the burnt area that we are grafting then heal quickly.”


V/O
The new theatres were recently handed over by the Making a Difference Trust to the Eastern Cape Minister of Health, Dr Phumza Dyantyi.

Phumza

“The work done by this trust throughout the country contributing to the improvement of public health service is truly commendable to receive this donation today on behalf of our province is such a great honour like a child excited to receive a gift from his/her parents I am extremely grateful and excited at the anticipation of the changes that this new paediatric theatre will bring to the Eastern Cape children.”

Up Sound Welcome

V/O
The transformation of this ward took 9 months and it could only have happened with the generous support of over 40 sponsors.

Up Sound They are state of art machine we could not ask for anything more.

V/O
Braam van der Hover was the architect.

“I think this is over and above the allowance of the private sector , it goes to the extent that this design goes to and the amount of equipment, you wouldn’t find a lot of facilities with these amentities in the private sector.”

“Welcome to this new paediatric operating theatre.”

V/O
The sponsors and delegates were taken on a tour of these impressive facilities.
Not only are there two operating theatres but an admission ward, a recovery ward and utility rooms.


V/O
The digital laparascopic operating theatre has all the bells and whistles any surgeon would hope for.

Dr Simango explains key hole surgery.

“He is projecting his fingers and you can see on our monitors this allows us to reduce abdominal surgery from a huge cut across your belly into a few tiny cuts.”

V/O
The second theatre is the general surgical theatre for less complicated cases.

Megan Coleman
“So this is a video loringascope, it uses video technology . There is a little video camera at the end here and that can actually go around corners and enable us to envisualise something that we wouldn’t normally be able to see.”

V/O
The facility has an invaluable tool of a digital clinical kiosk which can access all medical records of the patient for the doctors immediately.

Dr Simango
“We can take video clips, we can video conference when we want to and people are not in theatre with us can watch us from an adjoining room. All this we were not previously able to do in our old theatre .”

V/O
Prof Milind Chitnis is the head of the Paediatric surgical team.

“It is really impressive, it is not only of a national standard but of an international standard. Because most of my colleagues, me included we have worked overseas and the technology which we are able to use now. Latest technology which is available anywhere in the world.”

V/O
But all of this was made possible by sponsors with vision.

Sponsors
“Something like this for us where infants and children are able to get a second or even a third change in life resonated with us so much so that we felt that we wanted to be one of the initial partners with Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust.”

“It’s uplifting to see what can be done when different parties in the country work together.”

“Children are our future and we need to look after as best as we can.”

“So many children there is such a disconnect between access to health care and the availability to have a meaningful start to life so for us it’s a beautiful fit for what we believe in.”

It’s such an honour to be part of such a wonderful campaign that is making such a difference from the outset.”

V/O
Yolanda has just finished surgery and the doctors are optimistic about her road to recovery.

Up Sound Wake up girl

“I am hoping that the child will be alright.”

V/O
For those mother’s who have been on the waiting list for the past 5 months, they are unanimous in their appreciation that their children are in safe hands and have access to the care that they deserve.


Nozbeklelo Nkwana
“So the gift that these companies have given us, helps our children enormously. And I hope that they can continue and they should keep up their good work.”


Rolene
“You never know what that child is going to become one day. We don’t know what potential is sitting there. It could be the next Madiba. And so when you save that child’s life, you give them an opportunity to become a human being that fulfills their promise.”


Promo 1

Carte Blanche’s Making a Difference Trust recently handed over a state of the art Paediatric Facility to Frere Hospital in East London. The two digital operating theatres are providing first world care for our children.


Promo 2

Three years ago this was a disused operating theatre at Frere Hospital in East London. Today the Making a Difference Trust has spent 14 million rand and transformed it into these state of art operating theatres for children.
